# technitium_app (Resource)

Installs a DNS app and manages its config. Use `class_paths` in `technitium_dns_record_app`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "technitium_app" "split" {
  name = "Split Horizon"
  config = jsonencode({
    appPreference            = 40
    enableAddressTranslation = false
    networks                 = { lan = ["192.168.0.0/16"] }
    domainGroupMap           = {}
    networkGroupMap          = {}
    groups                   = []
  })
}

resource "technitium_dns_record_app" "www" {
  zone        = "example.com"
  name        = "www"
  app_name    = technitium_app.split.name
  class_path  = "SplitHorizon.SimpleAddress"
  record_data = jsonencode({ public = ["203.0.113.10"], private = ["192.168.1.10"] })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) App name, e.g. `Split Horizon`. Without `url` the app is installed from the DNS App Store by this name.

### Optional

- `config` (String) App config, usually JSON (`jsonencode(...)`). Compared as JSON, so formatting differences don't show as changes. Unset keeps the app's own config.
- `url` (String) `https://` URL of the app zip. Changing it updates the app in place. Omit to use the store's current version.

### Read-Only

- `class_paths` (List of String) Class paths of the app's handlers, e.g. `SplitHorizon.SimpleAddress`.
- `id` (String) App name; also the import ID.
- `version` (String) Installed version.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import technitium_app.split "Split Horizon"
```
